# python — three files, three extractors.
#
#   requirements.txt      declared requirements, pinned by ==  (python/requirements)
#   pyproject.toml        the project's own identity           (python/pyprojecttoml)
#   pylock/pylock.toml    PEP 751 resolved lockfile            (python/pylock)
#
# Fixture provenance — both new files are real, from the projects that generated
# them:
#   pylock/pylock.toml  pypa/pip's own build lockfile, build-project/pylock.toml
#     at b457f5ad0323454ec9f834e8297923d336ab164a (MIT), verbatim. Its published
#     wheel digests are what the pylock HashParser mines into component.hashes[].
#   pyproject.toml      pallets/flask's pyproject.toml at
#     6a2f545bfd8ed31e19066a299296917e034aca58 (BSD-3-Clause), trimmed to the
#     [project], [project.optional-dependencies] and [build-system] tables — the
#     tool-config tables the extractor never reads are dropped, the way the
#     kernel fixture keeps only the head of its vmlinuz.
#
# scalibr 87a1418f (2026-08-28) rewrote python/pyprojecttoml: it now emits only
# the project named in [project], carrying its declared dependencies as
# extractor metadata instead of as packages of their own (upstream 0419e25a then
# 73d42b53, "Align it with manifest-based extraction"). The eight declared-range
# components this fixture used to assert — blinker, click, itsdangerous, jinja2,
# markupsafe, werkzeug, asgiref, python-dotenv — are therefore no longer emitted
# by anything, and the project itself appears instead.
#
# The lockfile sits in a subdirectory on purpose. A lock's authority covers its
# own directory and below (internal/sbom/declared.go), so keeping it out of the
# fixture root leaves the root's declared requirements unsuppressed and all
# three extractors observable in one fixture. The suppression itself — a
# pyproject.toml whose deps its project's lock has already pinned — is unit
# tested, since want.txt can assert presence but not absence.
purl pkg:pypi/requests@2.31.0
cpe  cpe:2.3:a:requests:requests:2.31.0:*:*:*:*:*:*:*

# python/pylock — resolved pins, each carrying its wheel's SHA-256.
purl pkg:pypi/build@1.5.0
cpe  cpe:2.3:a:build:build:1.5.0:*:*:*:*:*:*:*
purl pkg:pypi/flit-core@3.12.0
cpe  cpe:2.3:a:flit-core:flit-core:3.12.0:*:*:*:*:*:*:*
purl pkg:pypi/packaging@26.2
cpe  cpe:2.3:a:packaging:packaging:26.2:*:*:*:*:*:*:*
purl pkg:pypi/pyproject-hooks@1.2.0
cpe  cpe:2.3:a:pyproject-hooks:pyproject-hooks:1.2.0:*:*:*:*:*:*:*

# python/pyprojecttoml — the [project] table's own name and version. Its
# declared dependencies now ride on the extractor's Metadata rather than
# becoming components, so nothing here asserts them.
purl pkg:pypi/flask@3.2.0.dev
cpe  cpe:2.3:a:flask:flask:3.2.0.dev:*:*:*:*:*:*:*
